blockers.summary: The reviewer wants the problem reproduced and understood from the boot side before accepting the patch. It is unclear that removing the fuseblk fallback is the right fix, especially since the original hanging-mount bug was reportedly resolved separately with mount namespaces.

The regression-potential section is factually wrong. os-prober is not simply disabled by default, because it is enabled automatically when other OSes are detected at install time. The section needs a real analysis of what the fuseblk fallback does and which filesystems or setups lose detection when it is removed (for example NTFS or other filesystems grub-probe can't identify).

The upload may be an unnecessary or conflicting change. The SRU says the hanging-mount fix is in Resolute but not backported to Noble and Jammy, and the mount-namespace approach may already have replaced the code being patched. The target series and the relationship to the existing fix are unclear, and the SRU depends on a later backport.

The test plan only covers the LVM snapshot case. It has no verification step showing the entries disappear after the fix, and no regression check that legitimate OSes on unusual filesystems are still detected.

autopkgtest failure/regression reported: "…e StableReleaseUpdates policy regarding autopkgtest regressions [1]. https://ubuntu-archive-team.ubuntu.com/proposed-migration/noble/updat…" (ubuntu-sru-bot)

Regression confirmed on a clean noble system: with ceph 19.2.6 from noble-proposed, libvirt RBD storage pools fail to start with 'failed to set RADOS option: auth_supported'. Ceph 19.2.6 removed that option, and noble's libvirt 10.0.0-2ubuntu8.19 still sets it. Nothing in the bug shows a libvirt SRU or a ceph compatibility patch being prepared, so the regression is unresolved.

The libvirt fix (a backport of upstream commit 3af8cc5) has been tested but has not been uploaded as a separate SRU. The reporter suggests releasing it before or together with ceph 19.2.6. That ordering needs coordination, and the libvirt change still needs its own SRU bug.

Release order and policy: 19.2.6 includes the CVE fix and CephX key handling changes, so the same fixes must be in resolute and stonking first (ceph 20.2.4, bug 2166817). The 20.2.4 package was still waiting in resolute unapproved as of the last update. The block-proposed-noble tag must stay until that lands.

The team is still working through decisions on how to communicate the change, on kernel implications of the CVE change, and on effects on other projects. The verification-done tag was removed and re-added while these are unresolved, so the tags may not reflect readiness to release.
The ubuntu-sru-bot reported an autopkgtest regression (libvirt on arm64) for the noble upload. No comment shows it was investigated or retried. It may be related to the auth_supported failure.

comments.author: whershberger
comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html

blockers.summary: Regression mentioned: "…to 64. This could produce a performance regression for some users, as the performance bottleneck of this cap was significant enoug…" (whershberger)

The backported patches parse /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, so get_global_pool_hard_max_size always returns the default and the limit never takes effect. The fix is only in upstream patches that are not yet merged, and it has not been added to the SRU.

The default hard max returned when the limit cannot be read is UINT_MAX. That is effectively unbounded, so the SRU does not cap the pool in that case. The proposed fix is the kernel default of 65530, and it is not yet merged upstream or included in the SRU.

The fix reads /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count, which needs a libvirt AppArmor profile change (LP #2170732). A versioned Breaks in qemu is also needed so libvirt gets upgraded. Neither is confirmed done, and without them confined guests may fail or behave differently after the upgrade.

The fix only reduces the chance of hitting vm.max_map_count and does not eliminate it. With enough vCPUs, such as 255, QEMU still crashes at the noble limit, and the behavior at the limit is not changed. The SRU should state this residual risk clearly.

The reproducer crashes the VM at the noble limit with 255 vCPUs. It is unclear whether the proposed package was tested at that scale, since the PPA result quoted is only 11507 VMAs, and the later string-parsing and default-limit fixes are not covered by that testing.
